claims.text: Premelting and melting behavior of high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles is governed by the interplay of compositional complexity, particle size, and surface energy.
Compositional complexity affects the thermal stability of high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
Particle size affects the thermal stability of high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
Surface energy affects the thermal stability of high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
Compositional complexity, particle size, and surface energy collectively affect nanoparticle phase transitions.
High-entropy-alloy nanoparticles have greater compositional complexity than pure-metal nanoparticles.
High-entropy-alloy nanoparticles have increased surface energy relative to pure-metal nanoparticles.
High-entropy-alloy nanoparticles exhibit suppressed premelting temperatures relative to pure-metal nanoparticles.
High-entropy-alloy nanoparticles exhibit suppressed melting temperatures relative to pure-metal nanoparticles.
The proposed temperature suppression is caused by increased compositional complexity and surface energy.
Nanoparticles varying in compositional complexity, particle size, and surface energy will be synthesized and compared under identical thermal conditions.
Pure-metal nanoparticles will serve as the comparison baseline.
The hypothesis applies across varying compositions, particle sizes, surface energies, temperatures, and heating rates.
The exact relationship among compositional complexity, particle size, surface energy, and thermal stability remains uncertain.
Independence of premelting and melting behavior from all three proposed governing variables would falsify the hypothesis.
